# Blues Flow

> Play and study 18 versions of the 12-bar blues, from three chords to Parker-style changes, in any key, with a walking-bass backing band.

By David Reinstein (https://www.davidreinstein.org/). More projects: https://projects.davidreinstein.org/

Free, no sign-up. A browser app (single page) for jazz and blues players learning blues changes.

## What it does

- Shows each of 18 twelve-bar blues forms as a lead sheet in any key, with chord names for concert, B-flat, E-flat or F instruments, roman numerals and guide tones (3rds and 7ths).
- Plays the form with a backing trio (piano comping, walking or two-feel bass, ride cymbal) at any tempo, with a count-in; can step through all 18 forms in turn.
- Marks which bars changed from the previous form and explains what each form adds.
- A flowchart of every chord option in every bar; click an option to swap it into the progression (mixes are kept in the URL).
- Printable posters of the forms in several keys, an audio file of all 18 forms with narration, and two YouTube videos (the 18 forms: https://youtu.be/hvldOdFz0wY, app tour: https://youtu.be/_ciNDOVZBzk).
- A vote on favourite forms and a form to suggest a new blues variation.
